name: Smith machine split squat
instructions: Set the Smith stops and bar across the upper back. Place the feet in a split stance suited to the rails, unlock and lower with both knees bending, then stand through the front leg.
notes: Keep both feet in place during reps. Test the rail path before loading. Record added plates only; exclude the Smith carriage rather than estimating its effective weight. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Smith machine rear-foot-elevated split squat
instructions: Place a stable bench behind the Smith bar and set stops. With the rear foot supported and bar on the upper back, lower through the front leg, then stand along the rail path. Change sides safely.
notes: Test bench distance and the unloaded path first. Do not let the bench move as you change stance. Record added plates only; exclude the Smith carriage rather than estimating its effective weight. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

variant.support: Smith bar and rear foot on bench

name: Front-foot-elevated dumbbell split squat
instructions: Hold equal dumbbells and place the front foot on a low stable platform with rear toes on the floor. Lower both knees through a controlled range, then stand through the front foot. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the entire front foot supported; extra depth is useful only while you can control it. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

variant.stance: stationary split stance front foot elevated

name: Dumbbell step-up
instructions: Hold equal dumbbells and place one whole foot on a stable platform. Stand through that leg to bring the body up, then lower the trailing foot back to the floor with control. Repeat on each side.
notes: Minimise push-off from the floor leg. One ascent and controlled return count as one rep for the leading leg. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Barbell step-up
instructions: Unrack a bar onto the upper back with a stable platform nearby. Plant one whole foot on the platform, stand through that leg, then lower carefully to the floor. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Use a modest platform height and clear route to the rack; avoid bouncing off the trailing leg. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Bodyweight step-up
instructions: Place one whole foot on a stable platform. Stand through that leg, bring the other foot up gently, then lower back to the floor with control. Repeat with the other leg leading.
notes: Count one ascent and return as one rep for the leading leg; use a height you can descend from smoothly. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Dumbbell lateral step-up
instructions: Stand beside a stable platform holding equal dumbbells. Place the nearer foot fully on top, rise through that leg, then lower the other foot back to the floor without dropping the hip. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the knee aligned with the working foot and avoid jumping off the floor leg. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Bodyweight step-down
instructions: Stand on a low platform on one leg. Bend that knee and hip to lower the free heel toward the floor in front, tap lightly, then rise through the platform leg. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep weight on the platform leg rather than pushing off the tapping heel; reduce height if the pelvis drops. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Dumbbell curtsy lunge
instructions: Hold equal dumbbells and take a small backward diagonal step behind the standing leg. Bend both knees through a comfortable range, then return through the front foot. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the pelvis controlled and the front knee tracking over the foot. Avoid a deep forced crossover or twisting through the knee. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Barbell hip thrust
instructions: Secure a bench and place a bar across the hip crease with upper back supported. With feet planted, lift the hips until the torso and thighs align, then lower under control without overextending the back.
notes: Keep the bench from sliding and use a comfortable bar pad. Record the bar and plates. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Dumbbell hip thrust
instructions: Rest the upper back against a secured bench and hold one dumbbell across the hip crease. Drive through both feet to raise the hips, then lower while keeping the weight stable with the hands.
notes: Use one dumbbell, not a pair. Finish with ribs down rather than arching above hip extension. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Smith machine hip thrust
instructions: Place a secured bench so the Smith bar sits comfortably over the hips. Set stops, support the upper back and unlock the bar, then raise and lower the hips along the rails.
notes: Check the unloaded path and bench clearance. Re-lock the bar before moving out. Record added plates only; exclude the Smith carriage rather than estimating its effective weight. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

variant.support: upper back on bench and Smith rails

name: Plate-loaded hip thrust machine
instructions: Adjust the back support and secure the machine hip restraint as directed. With both feet on the plate, extend the hips to raise the lever, then lower and secure the catch before getting out.
notes: Record added plates only. Lever ratios and starting resistance differ across models. Record the total plates added to all working levers, excluding the unloaded machine. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

variant.support: machine back pad and hip restraint

name: Bodyweight hip thrust
instructions: Rest the upper back against a stable bench with feet on the floor. Lift the hips until the thighs and torso align, pause with ribs down, then lower under control.
notes: No external load is required. Secure the bench so it cannot slide during the movement. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-leg bodyweight hip thrust
instructions: Support the upper back on a secured bench and lift one foot off the floor. Drive through the planted foot to raise the hips, keep the pelvis level and lower smoothly. Repeat on the other leg.
notes: Keep the free leg controlled; reduce range if the pelvis rotates. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Single-leg dumbbell hip thrust
instructions: Support the upper back on a stable bench and secure one dumbbell across the working hip crease. Lift the other foot, extend the planted-leg hip, then lower without rotating the pelvis. Repeat on the other leg.
notes: Keep one hand on the dumbbell to stop it rolling; use the same load on each side. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Barbell glute bridge
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent and a bar across the hip crease. Brace and press through both feet to lift the hips until torso and thighs align, then lower gently to the floor.
notes: Use a comfortable pad and a controlled way to position the bar. This floor-supported movement has less range than a bench hip thrust. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Dumbbell glute bridge
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent and hold one dumbbell across the hip crease. Press through both feet to lift the hips while keeping the ribs down, then lower without letting the weight roll.
notes: Record the single dumbbell weight. Keep the neck relaxed on the floor. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Bodyweight glute bridge
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet planted. Brace lightly, lift the hips until the thighs line up with the torso, then lower slowly while keeping the ribs from flaring.
notes: Avoid pushing through the neck or arching the lower back to gain extra height. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-leg bodyweight glute bridge
instructions: Lie on the floor with one foot planted and the other leg lifted. Raise the hips through the planted leg while keeping the pelvis level, then lower with control. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the free leg still rather than swinging it to help lift the hips. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Bodyweight frog pump
instructions: Lie on the floor with soles together and knees comfortably opened. Keep the feet close enough for control, lift the hips a short distance through hip extension, then lower without flaring the ribs.
notes: Use a comfortable hip opening; do not force the knees toward the floor. Each lift and lower is one rep. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Seated dumbbell lateral raise
instructions: Sit tall on a bench with dumbbells beside the thighs. Raise both arms out slightly forward of the sides with a small elbow bend, then lower without swinging the torso.
notes: Keep the seated position throughout; this is distinct from the existing standing lateral raise. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Leaning-away dumbbell lateral raise
instructions: Hold a secure rack with one hand and lean slightly away while holding a dumbbell in the other. Raise the working arm out to the side, then lower without changing the lean. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Use the rack for support rather than pulling on it to move the weight. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Side-lying incline dumbbell lateral raise
instructions: Lie on your side against an incline bench with a dumbbell beside the upper hip. Raise the upper arm away from the torso through a comfortable arc, then lower slowly. Change sides.
notes: Keep the torso supported and note the bench angle for comparable sessions. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell lateral raise
instructions: Lie chest down on a steep incline bench with the arms hanging beside the torso. Raise both dumbbells outward with elbows softly bent, then lower without lifting the chest off the pad.
notes: Use a steep incline and raise beside the torso; the flatter, rearward sweep belongs to a reverse fly. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Behind-the-body single-arm cable lateral raise
instructions: Stand side-on to a low pulley and take the handle in the farther hand with the cable passing behind the hips. Raise that arm outward, then return without twisting the trunk. Change sides.
notes: Use a comfortable starting position rather than forcing the arm far behind the torso. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Lateral raise machine
instructions: Adjust the seat so the shoulder area aligns with the machine pivots. Place the arms against the pads, raise them outward under control, then lower without dropping the stack.
notes: Use the same seat and pad settings when comparing sessions. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Bilateral cable lateral raise
instructions: Stand between two low pulleys holding the opposite handles with cables crossed in front. Raise both arms out to the sides with a small elbow bend, then lower smoothly.
notes: Use equal stack settings and record one working stack, not their sum. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Barbell front raise
instructions: Stand holding a barbell in front of the thighs with an overhand grip. Raise it forward to around shoulder height with softly bent elbows, then lower without leaning backward.
notes: Use a load that allows the torso to stay still. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Plate front raise
instructions: Hold a weight plate securely at its sides in front of the thighs. Raise it forward to around shoulder height, then lower under control with a small fixed elbow bend.
notes: Record the plate weight once, not once for each hand. Keep a secure grip throughout. Record the combined weight of the plates held by the working hand or hands, excluding bodyweight. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Simultaneous dumbbell front raise
instructions: Stand with equal dumbbells in front of the thighs. Raise both arms forward together to around shoulder height, then lower without rocking the body or shrugging the shoulders.
notes: One simultaneous lift and lower is one rep; use the existing alternating entry for alternating arms. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-arm cable front raise
instructions: Face away from a low cable with one handle beside the working thigh. Raise the arm forward through a comfortable arc, then lower slowly without letting the cable pull the torso back. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the elbow bend small and consistent. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Cable Y raise
instructions: Face two low pulleys holding their handles. With thumbs pointing upward, raise the arms diagonally into a Y without arching the back, then lower along the same path.
notes: Use a light load and allow the shoulder blades to move with the arms; this is not a shrug. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Incline dumbbell Y raise
instructions: Lie chest down on an incline bench with light dumbbells. Lift both arms diagonally forward into a Y with thumbs up, then lower while keeping the ribs against the pad.
notes: Use controlled shoulder-blade movement rather than lifting the head or extending the lower back. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation
instructions: Lie on your side with the upper elbow bent and resting against the torso. Hold a light dumbbell, rotate the forearm upward without moving the upper arm, then lower. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the elbow position fixed and use a comfortable rotation range. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Cable external rotation at side
instructions: Set the pulley near elbow height and hold the handle in the farther hand. Keep the elbow bent against the side, rotate the forearm outward, then return without turning the torso. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Use a light setting; the shoulder rotates while the upper arm stays beside the ribs. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Cable internal rotation at side
instructions: Set the pulley near elbow height and take the handle in the nearer hand. Hold the bent elbow against the side, rotate the forearm inward across the abdomen, then return. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the torso still and avoid pulling the elbow behind the ribs. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Dumbbell shrug
instructions: Stand holding equal dumbbells at the sides with arms long. Lift the shoulders upward without bending the elbows, pause briefly, then lower them smoothly.
notes: Do not roll the shoulders in circles or use knee drive to move the weights. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Barbell shrug
instructions: Hold a barbell in front of the thighs with straight arms. Raise the shoulders upward while standing tall, then lower under control without bending the elbows.
notes: Keep the bar close and the neck neutral; avoid rolling the shoulders backward. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Barbell curl
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with palms forward and elbows near the ribs. Curl by bending the elbows, then lower to a controlled arm extension without leaning backward.
notes: Choose a grip width that keeps the wrists comfortable. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: EZ-bar curl
instructions: Hold an EZ bar at the angled grips and stand tall. Curl the bar while keeping the upper arms near the sides, then lower without dropping or swinging the load.
notes: Include the actual EZ-bar mass in the recorded total; bar weights vary. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Barbell reverse curl
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with palms down and wrists straight. Bend the elbows to raise the bar without moving the upper arms forward, then lower slowly.
notes: Use a lighter load than a supinated curl and avoid letting the wrists fold. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: EZ-bar reverse curl
instructions: Hold the EZ bar overhand on its angled grips. Curl while keeping the upper arms steady and wrists aligned, then lower with control.
notes: Record the actual EZ-bar mass plus plates; keep the chosen grip consistent. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Alternating dumbbell curl
instructions: Stand with equal dumbbells at the sides. Curl one arm while turning its palm upward, lower it smoothly, then alternate arms without swinging the torso.
notes: Count reps separately for each arm, not as a combined alternating total. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Dumbbell hammer curl
instructions: Stand holding equal dumbbells with palms facing inward. Curl both weights together while keeping that grip and the upper arms still, then lower smoothly.
notes: Keep the wrists aligned with the forearms rather than tipping the weights inward. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Alternating dumbbell hammer curl
instructions: Hold equal dumbbells with palms facing each other. Curl one weight without moving the upper arm, lower it, then alternate to the other side while retaining the neutral grip.
notes: Count reps for each arm; both arms use the same dumbbell weight. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Cross-body dumbbell hammer curl
instructions: Hold one dumbbell at the side with palm inward. Bend the elbow to bring the weight diagonally toward the opposite chest, then lower without rotating the trunk. Complete both arms.
notes: Keep the movement controlled and the wrist neutral; do not swing across the body. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Seated dumbbell curl
instructions: Sit tall on a bench holding equal dumbbells with palms forward. Curl both weights without lifting the upper arms, then lower slowly while keeping the torso still.
notes: This entry uses simultaneous seated reps; use the alternating entry for alternating arms. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Incline dumbbell curl
instructions: Recline against an incline bench with the arms hanging beside the torso and palms forward. Curl both dumbbells without letting the elbows drift forward, then lower within a comfortable range.
notes: Keep bench angle consistent and avoid forcing the shoulders backward at the bottom. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Incline dumbbell hammer curl
instructions: Sit against an incline backrest with palms facing inward. Curl both dumbbells while keeping the upper arms beside the torso, then lower without changing the grip or arching off the pad.
notes: Use a comfortable shoulder position and keep the bench angle consistent. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Dumbbell concentration curl
instructions: Sit with feet apart and support the working upper arm against the inner thigh. Curl one dumbbell without moving that support point, then lower smoothly and repeat on the other arm.
notes: Do not use the thigh to bounce the weight upward. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Single-arm dumbbell preacher curl
instructions: Adjust a preacher bench so the upper arm rests on the pad. Curl one dumbbell with the shoulder supported, then lower without forcing the elbow into a locked position. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the upper arm on the pad throughout the repetition. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: EZ-bar preacher curl
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench with both upper arms supported and take the angled EZ grips. Curl the bar, then lower slowly without lifting the elbows or dropping into the bottom range.
notes: Include EZ-bar mass in the total and re-rack before leaving the seat. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Barbell spider curl
instructions: Lie chest down on an incline bench with the bar hanging below the shoulders. Bend the elbows to curl without moving the upper arms, then lower while keeping the chest supported.
notes: Arrange enough clearance for the bar and a controlled way to pick it up and set it down. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Dumbbell spider curl
instructions: Lie chest down on an incline bench with equal dumbbells hanging beneath the shoulders. Curl both weights with upper arms still, then lower without lifting the chest or swinging the elbows.
notes: Keep the palms forward and leave enough clearance below the bench. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Lying cable curl
instructions: Lie on your back with feet toward a low pulley and hold its bar with palms up. Keep the upper arms beside the torso, curl the handle toward the shoulders, then lower under control.
notes: Choose a distance that maintains cable tension without pulling you along the floor. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Standing cable-bar curl
instructions: Face a low pulley holding a straight bar with palms up. Keep elbows beside the ribs, curl the bar without leaning backward, then lower to a controlled arm extension.
notes: Keep the wrists straight rather than curling them to finish the movement. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Rope cable hammer curl
instructions: Hold a rope on a low pulley with palms facing inward. Bend both elbows to raise the rope ends without moving the upper arms, then lower while keeping the grip neutral.
notes: Record the single stack setting, not a separate load for each rope end. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-arm cable curl
instructions: Face a low pulley with one handle and palm forward. Keep the working elbow beside the torso, curl toward the shoulder, then lower without rotating the body. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the upper arm steady rather than reaching the shoulder forward. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Behind-the-body cable curl
instructions: Face away from a low pulley and hold its handle with the upper arm slightly behind the torso. Curl by bending the elbow, then return without letting the cable pull the shoulder farther back. Repeat on both sides.
notes: Use a comfortable shoulder extension and avoid an exaggerated stretch. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: High-cable double-biceps curl
instructions: Stand between two pulleys set near head height and hold equal handles with arms out to the sides. Curl the hands toward the head while keeping the upper arms steady, then extend slowly.
notes: Use equal stack settings and record one stack. Do not turn the movement into a pulldown. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Preacher curl machine
instructions: Adjust the seat so the elbows align with the machine pivots and upper arms rest on the pad. Curl the handles, then lower smoothly without lifting the arms or slamming the stack.
notes: Keep the chosen seat and grip settings consistent. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Dumbbell Zottman curl
instructions: Curl both dumbbells with palms up. At the top, turn the palms downward, lower slowly with that overhand grip, then turn back at the bottom before the next curl.
notes: One up-and-down cycle is one rep; choose a load you can lower in the pronated grip. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Rope triceps pushdown
instructions: Face a high pulley holding the rope ends beside the chest. Keep the upper arms near the ribs, straighten both elbows, then return without letting the shoulders swing forward.
notes: Separate the ends only as far as comfortable; record the working stack once. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Straight-bar triceps pushdown
instructions: Take an overhand grip on a high-pulley bar. Hold the upper arms still beside the torso, extend the elbows to press down, then bend them to return under control.
notes: Keep the wrists aligned and avoid leaning bodyweight onto the bar. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Reverse-grip triceps pushdown
instructions: Hold a high-pulley bar with palms up and elbows near the ribs. Straighten the elbows while keeping the grip secure, then return slowly without moving the upper arms.
notes: Use a light enough setting to keep the wrists comfortable; an underhand grip does not isolate a separate triceps head. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-arm cable triceps pushdown
instructions: Face a high pulley holding one handle with the working elbow beside the ribs. Straighten that elbow, then return with the upper arm still. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Avoid rotating the torso or pushing the shoulder down to move the stack. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Cross-body cable triceps extension
instructions: Stand side-on to a high pulley with the farther hand holding the handle across the upper torso. Keep the upper arm steady and extend the elbow diagonally across and down, then return. Repeat on both sides.
notes: Choose the cable height and arm position for a comfortable elbow path; do not rotate the trunk to finish. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Overhead rope cable triceps extension
instructions: Face away from a pulley holding the rope behind the head with upper arms raised. Brace and extend both elbows, then bend them to lower the hands without flaring the ribs.
notes: Set the pulley so the cable follows a comfortable line behind the upper arms; use one stack setting. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-arm overhead cable triceps extension
instructions: Hold one cable handle behind the head with the upper arm raised. Keep the torso braced, straighten the working elbow, then bend it to return. Repeat on the other arm.
notes: Do not arch the lower back to gain overhead range. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Lying cable triceps extension
instructions: Place a bench with the head toward a low pulley and lie holding its bar above the shoulders. Keep the upper arms steady, bend the elbows to bring the bar toward the head, then extend.
notes: Position the bench and cable before loading and keep the bar clear of the face. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: EZ-bar lying triceps extension
instructions: Lie on a bench holding an EZ bar above the shoulders. Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward or just behind the forehead, then straighten them while keeping the upper arms controlled.
notes: Use a secure grip and arrange assistance for heavy setups. Include the actual EZ-bar weight in the total. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Barbell lying triceps extension
instructions: Lie on a bench with a barbell held above the shoulders. Bend the elbows to lower the bar through a comfortable path near the head, then extend without turning the movement into a press.
notes: Choose a wrist-friendly grip and use assistance when positioning or removing the bar. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Dumbbell lying triceps extension
instructions: Lie on a bench holding equal dumbbells above the shoulders with palms facing inward. Bend both elbows to lower the weights beside the head, then straighten them without swinging the upper arms.
notes: Keep the dumbbells clear of the face and record one dumbbell weight. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Rolling dumbbell triceps extension
instructions: Lie on a bench with equal dumbbells above the chest. Bend the elbows and let the upper arms roll back slightly, then reverse the arc and extend the elbows to return.
notes: This entry includes deliberate upper-arm movement, unlike a fixed-arm lying extension. Keep the rolling range controlled. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Seated dumbbell overhead triceps extension
instructions: Sit tall holding one dumbbell securely overhead with both hands. Bend the elbows to lower it behind the head, then straighten them while keeping the torso braced.
notes: Record the single dumbbell weight; keep a secure two-hand grip during setup and return. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-arm dumbbell overhead triceps extension
instructions: Hold one dumbbell overhead with the upper arm controlled near the head. Bend the elbow to lower the weight behind you, then extend without arching the back. Repeat on the other arm.
notes: Use a comfortable shoulder position; the free hand may steady the working upper arm. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Single-arm dumbbell triceps kickback
instructions: Support the free hand on a bench and hinge with the working upper arm beside the torso. Straighten that elbow to move the dumbbell back, then bend it slowly without dropping the upper arm.
notes: Keep the shoulder still rather than swinging the entire arm. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Single-arm cable triceps kickback
instructions: Face a low pulley in a hip hinge with one handle and the working upper arm beside the torso. Extend the elbow backward, then return while keeping the upper arm in place. Repeat on both sides.
notes: Keep the trunk braced and the cable clear of the legs. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Triceps extension machine
instructions: Adjust the seat and upper-arm pads so the elbows align with the machine pivots. Extend both elbows against the handles, then return slowly while keeping the arms supported.
notes: This entry is an elbow-extension machine, not a seated dip-press machine. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Barbell JM press
instructions: Lie on a bench with a comfortably close barbell grip. Lower toward the upper chest by bending the elbows and letting them move slightly forward, then extend and press back to the start.
notes: Use a light load and safeties while learning the hybrid path; do not lower the bar onto the neck. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Bodyweight triceps dip
instructions: Support yourself on secure parallel bars with arms straight. Keep the torso relatively upright, bend the elbows to lower through a comfortable shoulder range, then press back up without swinging.
notes: Do not force a deep bottom position; this is not a bench dip. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Weighted triceps dip
instructions: Secure added weight to a dip belt and support yourself on parallel bars. Lower with a relatively upright torso and controlled elbows, then press back to straight arms without swinging the weight.
notes: Record added load separately from bodyweight and keep plates clear of surrounding equipment. Record added weight separately from optional bodyweight. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Assisted dip machine
instructions: Select assistance and mount the dip machine as directed. Hold the handles with torso relatively upright, lower through a comfortable range, then press up without bouncing the support pad.
notes: Record positive assistance, not added load. More assistance makes the movement easier. Record the displayed assistance as a positive amount, separately from optional bodyweight. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Close-grip push-up
instructions: Start in a firm plank with hands comfortably closer than a standard push-up. Bend the elbows close to the torso to lower the chest, then press up while keeping the body aligned.
notes: The hands need not touch. Choose a position that keeps the wrists and elbows comfortable. Log repetitions; recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Seated barbell wrist curl
instructions: Sit with forearms supported on the thighs and palms up holding a barbell beyond the knees. Flex the wrists to raise the bar through a small arc, then lower with the forearms still.
notes: Keep the bar secure in the fingers rather than rolling it out of the hands. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Seated barbell reverse wrist curl
instructions: Sit with forearms supported on the thighs and palms down holding a light barbell. Extend the wrists to lift the knuckles, then lower slowly without moving the elbows.
notes: Use a small comfortable range and keep the grip secure. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Single-arm dumbbell wrist curl
instructions: Support one forearm on the thigh with palm up and wrist just beyond the knee. Curl one dumbbell using the wrist alone, then lower slowly. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Keep the forearm supported and do not roll the dumbbell out of the fingers. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Single-arm dumbbell reverse wrist curl
instructions: Support the forearm on the thigh with palm down and a light dumbbell beyond the knee. Lift the back of the hand through wrist extension, then lower with control. Repeat on the other side.
notes: Do not lift the whole forearm to compensate for a heavy weight. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Seated cable wrist curl
instructions: Sit facing a low pulley holding its bar with palms up and forearms on the thighs. Flex the wrists to draw the bar upward, then return slowly while the elbows stay still.
notes: Set the seat distance to maintain cable tension without pulling the forearms off their support. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Seated cable reverse wrist curl
instructions: Sit facing a low pulley holding the bar palms down with forearms supported on the thighs. Lift the knuckles through wrist extension, then lower without moving the elbows.
notes: Use a light stack setting and keep the wrists within a comfortable range. Record the displayed setting of the working stack. For two independent stacks, use equal settings and record ONE stack, not their sum. One complete bilateral movement counts as one rep.

name: Dumbbell forearm pronation
instructions: Support the forearm with the elbow bent and hold a light dumbbell near one end. Start with the weighted end upright, rotate toward palm-down under control, then return to upright. Repeat on both sides.
notes: Record the dumbbell mass and note grip position; changing the lever length changes difficulty without changing weight. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Dumbbell forearm supination
instructions: Support the forearm with elbow bent and hold a light dumbbell near one end. Start with the weighted end upright, rotate toward palm-up through a comfortable arc, then return. Repeat on both sides.
notes: Keep the elbow still. Record mass and grip position rather than treating different lever lengths as equal resistance. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Dumbbell wrist radial deviation
instructions: Support the forearm with the thumb facing upward and hold a light dumbbell near one end. Tilt the wrist toward the thumb side to raise the weighted end, then lower without moving the forearm. Repeat on both sides.
notes: Use a short controlled range and note grip position because lever length affects difficulty. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.

name: Dumbbell farmer hold
instructions: Stand tall holding equal dumbbells at the sides with arms long. Keep the weights still and wrists neutral for the planned time, then set them down under control.
notes: Hold in place; this entry measures time, not carry distance. Record one dumbbell weight. Record the weight of one dumbbell; use equal dumbbells for two-arm sets. Log hold duration in seconds; repetitions do not apply.

name: Dumbbell suitcase hold
instructions: Stand with one dumbbell beside the thigh and shoulders level. Hold without leaning or letting the wrist fold, then set it down safely and repeat on the other side.
notes: Duration is per side. Use equal hold times; log sides as separate sets with side notes if they differ. Record the weight of the single dumbbell used. Log hold duration in seconds; repetitions do not apply.

name: Double-overhand barbell hold
instructions: Set a bar on rack pins near standing hand height. Grip it with both palms down, lift just clear of the pins and hold with straight arms, then return it gently to the supports.
notes: Use a double-overhand grip without straps for consistent grip tracking. This measures hold time, not repetitions. Record the total barbell load, including the bar and plates. Log hold duration in seconds; repetitions do not apply.

name: Single-hand plate pinch hold
instructions: Pinch a suitable plate or matching smooth-sided plates between the thumb and fingers of one hand. Lift clear of the floor, hold without resting against the leg, then set down and change hands.
notes: Duration is per hand. Record the combined plate mass in the working hand and note plate thickness; keep the drop area clear. Record the combined weight of the plates held by the working hand or hands, excluding bodyweight. Log hold duration in seconds; repetitions do not apply.

name: Dead hang
instructions: Take a secure overhand grip on a pull-up bar with room for the feet to clear. Hang with straight elbows in a comfortable shoulder position for the planned time, then step down under control.
notes: This is a timed hang, not scapular pull-up repetitions. Avoid forcing a painful passive shoulder range. Recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. Log hold duration in seconds; repetitions do not apply.

name: Towel hang
instructions: Drape a strong training towel over a secure pull-up bar and grip both hanging ends. Lift the feet to hang with straight elbows, hold without swinging, then step down safely.
notes: Check towel condition and anchoring before loading it. Duration is for the two-hand hold; do not use a damaged towel. Recording bodyweight is optional. Do not enter bodyweight as external load. Log hold duration in seconds; repetitions do not apply.

name: Hand-gripper close
instructions: Place a hand gripper securely in one hand. Squeeze through its controlled closing range, then reopen slowly without dropping it. Complete the planned repetitions and repeat with the other hand.
notes: Count full closes consistently; keep model and resistance setting in notes rather than comparing nominal ratings as equivalent loads. Log full close-and-release repetitions. Record gripper model and resistance setting in workout notes; do not invent a kilogram value. Reps are per side. Use the same reps on each side; log sides separately if they differ.
